claims.text: A thin, dense ZrN coating on zirconium-alloy cladding will significantly improve high-temperature oxidation resistance.
ZrN-coated zirconium-alloy cladding will retain suitability for service.
The ZrN coating acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
The proposed coating is sub-micrometer in thickness and approximately 1 μm thick.
The ZrN coating will be deposited by a high-temperature CVD process involving surface cleaning, activation, and controlled deposition.
The proposed CVD process will form a dense, adherent nitride layer.
The coating is expected to be effective in high-temperature steam environments representative of accident scenarios.
Exposure at approximately 1200°C in steam for 30 minutes represents the regime of interest.
A dense ZrN layer limits oxygen ingress toward the underlying zirconium alloy.
ZrN's chemical inertness minimizes further oxidation reactions at the coating–substrate interface.
A chemically stable and structurally continuous ZrN barrier reduces oxygen diffusion into the cladding.
Reduced oxygen diffusion decreases the formation rate of detrimental zirconium oxide scale.
Compared with uncoated cladding under identical conditions, ZrN-coated cladding will have a significantly lower oxidation rate.
Compared with the uncoated baseline, ZrN-coated cladding will exhibit reduced weight gain after high-temperature steam exposure.
Compared with the uncoated baseline, ZrN-coated cladding will develop a thinner oxide scale.
The hypothesis does not address long-term in-reactor performance or irradiation effects.
Long-term mechanical stability and adhesion under reactor irradiation are uncertain.
ZrN coating performance during thermal cycling is uncertain.
Coated and uncoated specimens will be compared after exposure to steam at 1200°C for 30 minutes using weight gain, oxide thickness, SEM, and EDS.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant reduction in weight gain or oxide thickness, or barrier-compromising delamination or degradation, will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The coating is described as sub-micrometer while also specified as approximately 1 μm; 1 μm is not strictly below one micrometer.
